app.title: Causal Method Advisor
app.summary: A person picks a demo dataset or uploads a CSV, previews it, and types a causal question in plain language. The advisor profiles the data and shows how it read the question: question type, treatment, outcome, instrument, mediator, threshold variable, whether assignment was randomized, and whether a hidden confounder is suspected. If it is unsure of a role, it says which one. The person corrects or confirms these roles and re-runs. They then get a recommendation, several options, or a refusal, with an explanation, a calibrated confidence and scores for the top methods. Below that come the assumption checks behind the advice, reference cards for the leading methods, and a table of every method the rules allowed, flagged or ruled out, with reasons.

task.text: Choose the causal inference method that fits a question and a dataset, after checking how the question was read and which assumptions the data supports.

data.text: A tabular dataset (cross-sectional rows, a panel of units over time, or a single time series) together with a free-text question; the interface gives columns roles and computes diagnostics and method scores.
data.item: a dataset paired with one causal question, whose columns are given roles such as treatment and outcome

stage.text: choosing an estimation method for a causal question once the data is in hand, before estimating the effect

mechanism.text: A question box and a dataset feed an advisor that fills a role form, which the person corrects and re-runs. The corrected roles then drive the advice panel, the assumption-check list and the method cards below it. Rules remove methods the data cannot support, and a confidence score decides whether the advice is one recommendation, several options or a refusal.

field.text: choosing a causal inference method in statistics and econometrics

workflow.name: choose an analysis method that fits a question and a dataset

steps.here: a radio switches between a demo dataset (which fills in its own question) and a CSV upload; an expander previews the first 20 rows with the row and column counts

steps.step: state the question to be answered
steps.here: a free-text question in English or Russian, sent with the Advise button; the sidebar chooses which model reads it

steps.step: check and correct how the question was read
steps.here: dropdowns of this CSV's columns for treatment, outcome, instrument, mediator and threshold variable, plus question type, randomized and hidden confounder; the least certain role is marked 'please check', and 'Re-run with these roles' recomputes

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: assumption checks (parallel pre-trends, synthetic-control fit, overlap and balance, instrument strength, threshold variable, nonlinearity, non-Gaussian noise) are listed with their flags, and the data profile the model sees can be opened

steps.step: reach the recommendation, with its confidence
steps.here: a badge for recommend, options or refuse; an explanation; a calibrated confidence in the top method; score bars for up to five methods; the badge says 'provisional' while roles are unconfirmed
expanders for the top three methods show the estimand, assumptions, Python libraries and sources, and a table lists every method as allowed, warning or forbidden, with the reasons

distinctive: Hard rules rule out methods the data structure cannot support (no time column, no controls, continuous treatment) before the remaining methods are ranked.
The advice switches between one recommendation, several options and a refusal using a calibrated confidence, not a fixed rule.
A separate confidence in how the question was read names the least certain role, and the advice stays provisional until the person confirms it.
An instrument or mediator read from the question is stated in words for the person to check, because the data cannot tell the two apart.
The model's explanation is shown only if every number in it matches the diagnostics; otherwise a template explanation is used and the screen says so.
